prompt: Recreate, from scratch, a rainstorm against a window at night as a single self-contained HTML page with a canvas animation. We are indoors looking out at a dark town: wind-driven rain falls in depth layers, the near sheet fast and bright right against the glass, the far wall of rain slow and washed out, every streak leaning the same way under one gale. Water clings to the glass itself - beads of condensation sit still until a droplet creeps down through them in stick-slip runs, swallowing each bead it passes so it grows as it goes and never runs back up. Low in the pane a puddle line catches the downpour and throws small splashes back above it. Every few seconds lightning fires on a fixed schedule, briefly lights the whole scene, and decays away to nothing before the next one. Write your own implementation; do not copy any existing code.
definition_of_done:
final_output_file: rain-window.html, one self-contained HTML page. All cases in test_acceptance.py pass via `python -I -m unittest discover -s . -v` with exit code 0. Every sentence below is measured, not asserted.
1. The page starts with <!doctype html> and contains a <canvas>.
2. It makes ZERO external requests: no http(s) src or href, no @import, no url(//...), no fetch, no XMLHttpRequest. Everything is inline.
3. It drives the animation with requestAnimationFrame.
4. All of the maths lives in <script id="storm-model" type="module"> exporting a PURE function `step(t)` for time t in seconds. That block is run on its own in node by the gate, so it must not mention getContext, document., window. or canvas anywhere - pure numbers only. The renderer is a separate script that calls it.
5. step(t) returns {width, height, puddleY, drops, runners, splashes, flash}. step(0).drops holds 200 to 20000 streaks; every streak has finite numeric x, y, len, vx, vy and an INTEGER layer; len and vy are strictly positive; there are at least 3 distinct layers and no layer holds less than 5% of the streaks.
6. Depth reads as speed: sorting the layers by their index, mean vy rises strictly with the index, and the nearest layer falls at least 1.3x as fast as the farthest.
7. The rain is wind-driven: every vx has the same sign (one gale, one direction), and in the nearest layer mean |vx| is at least 0.1x mean vy, so the rain visibly leans.
8. puddleY sits between 0.5 and 0.97 of the height. No streak falls more than 2px past it, none starts higher than -0.5x the height, and none blows outside -0.5x to 1.5x the width.
9. At every quarter second from 0 to 24s, step(t).runners holds 3 to 400 droplets, each with an INTEGER id, a positive radius r, x inside the pane and y on the glass above puddleY.
10. Droplets only ever run downward: for any id present in two consecutive quarter-second samples, y never decreases; and over those 24s at least 5 droplets travel more than 15px.
11. Droplets merge: for any id present in two consecutive samples, r never decreases, and r grows on at least 3 occasions within those 24s.
12. step(t).splashes are pinned to the water line: the count peaks at 3 or more, it varies over time, and no splash sits more than 60px above puddleY or more than 8px below it.
13. step(t).flash stays within 0..1, drops below 0.05 between strikes, and sampled every 0.05s over 60s gives at least 3 strikes above 0.6 whose onsets are on a schedule: every gap is within 10% of the mean gap.
14. Each strike decays: it peaks above 0.6, is down to a quarter of that peak 1.5s later, and is below 0.1 by 2.5s.
If the contract cannot be satisfied, return status='failure' with the precise reason rather than a page that games the tests.
contract:
Return ONE complete HTML document in the `code` field, from <!doctype html> to </html>. Structure it as model plus renderer.
1. <script id="storm-model" type="module"> holds ONLY pure maths and exports `step(t)`. The gate extracts this block, writes it to model.mjs and runs it standalone in node, then greps it for getContext, document., window. and canvas - none of those words may appear in it, in code or in a comment.
   step(t) returns an object with:
   - width, height: the scene size in px. puddleY: the water line, low in the pane.
   - drops: an array of falling streaks, each {x, y, len, vx, vy, layer} with layer an integer index, 0 = farthest. x and y are scene px, y grows downward, vx and vy are px/s.
   - runners: an array of droplets on the glass, each {id, x, y, r} with id an integer that identifies one droplet over time. A droplet that reaches the bottom or is absorbed leaves the array; a newly released droplet takes a NEW id.
   - splashes: an array of {x, y} sitting on or just above puddleY.
   - flash: one number in 0..1, the lightning intensity at time t.
   Model requirements: per-layer fall speed rising with the layer index (near falls faster than far); a single signed wind ratio applied to every streak so vx never changes sign; droplet y a MONOTONE non-decreasing function of the droplet's age, so no droplet can run back up the glass; droplet radius accumulated from the beads it has passed, so it only ever grows; lightning on a fixed period with a decaying flash. Deterministic for a given t: the gate calls step at fixed times and compares the results, so no Math.random and no clock.
2. A separate <script> owns the <canvas>, sizes it to the viewport, and on each requestAnimationFrame calls step(elapsedSeconds) and draws it. The model block cannot be imported by URL, so read its textContent and evaluate it - a Blob plus dynamic import() is the way, and it stays offline.
Render requirements: a night-dark town behind the rain; rain drawn back to front with the far layers thinner and dimmer than the near ones; droplets on the glass rendered as refracting beads with a highlight, runners leaving a wet trail; a puddle band with splashes and spreading rings; the lightning brightening the sky, the rain and the glass together; a window frame and vignette. Everything inline: no external fonts, images, scripts, stylesheets or network calls of any kind.
